what_it_does: Gently exfoliates and hydrates while supporting a smoother, brighter-looking skin surface.
summary_short: Gluconolactone is a polyhydroxy acid (PHA) that exfoliates more gently than many AHAs. It also helps attract water, making it a good option for dull, uneven, or sensitive skin that may not tolerate stronger acids.
summary_long:
Gluconolactone is a polyhydroxy acid, or PHA. Like alpha hydroxy acids, it helps loosen the bonds between dead surface skin cells so they shed more evenly, which can make skin look smoother, brighter, and less flaky over time.

Because gluconolactone has a larger molecular size than common AHAs like glycolic acid, it is generally considered slower-penetrating and often gentler. This does not make it irritation-proof, but it may be better tolerated by sensitive, dry, or redness-prone skin than stronger exfoliating acids.

Gluconolactone also has humectant properties, meaning it can help draw water into the upper layers of skin. It is sometimes described as having antioxidant-supporting properties, though the visible skincare benefits are best understood as gentle exfoliation plus hydration support.

In leave-on skincare, gluconolactone is commonly used around 2–10%, while stronger exfoliating products may use higher levels. The overall formula matters: pH, other acids, alcohol content, and frequency of use can all change how gentle or irritating a product feels.

Start slowly if your skin is sensitive or if you already use retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, vitamin C acids, or other exfoliants. It pairs well with barrier-supporting ingredients like glycerin, hyaluronic acid, ceramides, panthenol, and niacinamide. Daily sunscreen is still important, especially when using exfoliating products.
quick_facts: Good for dull or rough texture
